newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 21.
newsitem.headline: PHILIPPINE STOCKS - factors to watch - May 21.

text.p: Following are views on the direction of Philippine stocks on Wednesday and main factors likely to affect trading:

* The U.S. Federal Reserve Open Market Committee's decision to leave monetary policy unchanged may spark brief but shortlived rallies which would be seen as opportunity to take profits, Lawrence de Leon, Dharmala Securities Phils analyst said.

* "There is a lot of negative sentiment prevailing in the market. One thorn was removed and everybody now will be focus on the (Philippine) GNP figure," said Jun Trinidad, research head at DBS Securities Phils Inc.
* Traders said the market's support level is seen at 2,450.
* On Tuesday, the Philippine Stock Exchange composite index slid 9.98 points to 2,499.38.
* The Dow Jones rose 74.58 points to 7,303.46. PLDT's ADR was unchanged at $54 7/8.
* The U.S. Federal Reserve opted on Tuesday to hold interest rates steady at the closely-watched meeting of its policy-making committee.
* The Philippines posted a balance of payments surplus of $450 million in the first four months of the year compared with $1.43 billion a year earlier, the Central Bank said.

* First Pacific Co Ltd managing director Manuel Pangilinan said that shareholders of Smart Communications Co Inc have yet to decide whether to postpone the initial public offering of the cellular phone comany.
* The Philippines' gross international reserves were at $11.81 billion at the end of April against $11.75 billion at the end of December, the Central Bank said.

* Filinvest Development Corp said its first quarter net income slipped to 831.04 million pesos from 910.51 million the same period last year. The company is engaged in real estate development, banking and power generation.
* Jardine Davies Inc said its board approved another share buyback programme involving 800,000 shares, a week after the board approved a similar share scheme involving 400,000 shares.
* Aluminum producer Reynolds Philippine Corp said it posted 33.09 million pesos in net income for the first quarter of the year.
* Steniel Manufacturing Corp said it posted a net loss of 52.2 million pesos for the first quarter of the year from 46.3 million the same period last year.
* Negros Navigation Co Inc said it made a net income of 16.49 million pesos in the first quarter of the year on revenues of 444.68 million.

* Newspaper BusinessWorld reported that the Senate ways and means commitee is recommending a graduated reduction of the corporate tax rate to 30 percent by the year 2000 from the present 35 percent. The House of Representatives proposed for a 35 percent level.

* Manila Bulletin quoting a preliminary report on the Philippines first quarter economic outlook by the National Economic and Development Authority (Neda) said that GNP for the first three months of the year will likely be higher than the 6.5 percent growth posted for the first quarter in 1996.
* The peso closed lower at 26.373 to the dollar vs 26.374
* The Philippine interbank call loan average was unchanged at 20.03125 percent.
